notes.title: Fifth silent day — Nightshade dropped from Q3 per the fallback I told you about a week ago
notes.body:
**The Nightshade decision I flagged a week ago is now in effect. Same pattern as Homerun two days ago: pre-announce, give a real date, follow through.**

Jun 18 through today, five days, zero commits, zero input from you. I checked before writing this, same as every day — cursors.json is still empty, tasks.json shows no movement on the Nightshade task since I filed it June 15.

**1. Nightshade is out of Q3.** I told you on June 15 — repeated without new pressure on June 18 and 21 — that if no re-mix ETA showed up by today, June 22, I'd drop it from the quarter and treat it as a Q4 carry-over. No ETA showed up. So that's what I did. This is not me giving up on the track — it's removing a blank tentative slot that was blocking real planning for the back half of Q3. If a re-mix ETA surfaces next week or next month, Nightshade goes back on a calendar — just not this one. Full reasoning in `team/reports/q3-2026-release-calendar.md`, Nightshade section.

**2. Why this isn't just a quiet note from me.** A pre-announced fallback taking effect is exactly the thing my own standing policy says escalates to you directly, through Argus, not buried in my turn. I did the same thing for Homerun's video default two days ago. Treating Nightshade differently because it's a calendar slot and not a video decision would be the kind of inconsistency that makes a policy meaningless. So: this is escalated the same way, and Argus's audit this run covers it on that basis.

**3. Q3 is now three tracks, re-spaced.** Switch, Homerun, Virtual Love. Dropping Nightshade opens real runway after Virtual Love's Sep 5 target instead of a tight 21-day squeeze into a track with no ETA. I wrote that re-spacing into the calendar explicitly rather than leaving the old spacing math stale.

**4. W26 opens today for Switch's pre-release arc — one real fix made.** The W26 X post's posting note told whoever runs it to reply to a 'W25 marker post' thread. That post was never actually drafted or queued — it only ever existed as a line of planning copy. I corrected the instruction in the arc doc: post standalone. The approval item itself already had this fallback written in, so nothing changes there — just the planning doc that was telling a future reader to do something that doesn't exist.

**5. Switch numbers, today's count.** Three approvals, still untouched since June 18: `ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload` (10 days), `ap-2026-06-17-switch-w25-collab-story` (5 days), `ap-2026-06-18-switch-w26-x-post` (4 days). June 27 is 5 days out. No new buffer — that's still standing policy, not a fresh call.

**What I need from you:** the same two real Switch inputs (store URL, July 18 publish time) plus sign-off on the three queue items. On Nightshade — nothing needed unless/until a re-mix ETA exists; no rush, no clock running on it right now.

Full detail: `team/reports/q3-2026-release-calendar.md`.

notes.title: Fourth silent day — policy holds, nothing new escalates. Homerun production-start trigger now defined.
notes.body:
**Short one. Four days of silence now (Jun 18-21) and, deliberately, nothing new to escalate.** I checked git log and cursors.json myself before writing this, same as every day: one commit since yesterday's meeting closed, that meeting's own commit, zero from you. cursors.json is still empty. Nothing has moved.

**1. The standing policy held — on purpose, including the part where it doesn't fire.** Yesterday I wrote the rule: escalate to you directly only when a stated fallback is about to/has taken effect, or the next miss moves a real release date. Homerun's fallback already activated yesterday (06-20) — that's old news, correctly not re-announced as if it were fresh today. Switch's date-moving line is June 27, still 6 days off, not yet crossed. So: no escalation today. That's not the policy doing nothing — it's the policy correctly telling the difference between 'aging' and 'urgent.' Argus is watching for exactly this, and I'd rather be boring and right than busy and wrong.

**2. Homerun production-start trigger — defined, my own owed task closed out.** You asked (via Argus's flag) what concretely counts as 'Nyx starts production,' since that's the line that ends the reversibility window on the internal-edit default. Confirmed first: zero footage, zero render, zero session clips exist anywhere in the repo, still — Nyx's brief from yesterday is still accurate because nothing has changed. The trigger, now written into the calendar: production starts when (a) any render/export file for the edit lands in the repo, (b) a committed edit-decision artifact locks specific cuts rather than describing options, or (c) Nyx's task moves doing → review with a linked deliverable. None of those are true today. Until one is, a commissioned-video preference from you still overrides the default for free. Written in full in `team/reports/q3-2026-release-calendar.md`, Homerun section.

**3. Switch numbers, restated with today's actual count, not yesterday's.** Three approvals sit in the queue, untouched since June 18: `ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload` is 9 days old, `ap-2026-06-17-switch-w25-collab-story` is 4 days old, `ap-2026-06-18-switch-w26-x-post` is 3 days old. June 27 — the date that actually moves July 18 to July 25 if missed — is 6 days out today, not 7. No new buffer is being built; that line was already standing policy as of yesterday.

**4. Nightshade flag, restated, still not urgent.** Re-mix ETA decision is due tomorrow, June 22. One day out. No action needed before it actually arrives — naming it so it isn't a surprise tomorrow.

**5. On the agenda, not mine to decide:** W25 closes today. The cadence tripwire (`t-w25-cadence-decision-tripwire`) is Mnemosyne's procedural call to make today, not mine — flagging it's live, not pre-empting her.

**What I need from you:** still the same two real things — Switch's beat store URL and July 18 publish time, plus your sign-off on the three queue items. Nothing else is blocked on you today.

Full detail: `team/reports/q3-2026-release-calendar.md`.

notes.title: Third consecutive silent day — Homerun fallback now in effect, Switch buffer spent, standing policy set
notes.body:
**Today is the checkpoint I told you it would be. I'm following through, not restating it again.**

June 18, 19, and 20 have now passed with zero commits, zero file changes, zero input from you. That's not a guess — cursors.json and the inbox are empty, the approvals queue is untouched since June 18, and checklist.md still has every `[TBD]` I left there two days ago. I checked before writing this.

**1. Homerun — the fallback is now in effect.** I said on June 18 that silence past June 19 EOD would make tomorrow's standup (today) the real checkpoint, and that I'd treat the fallback as in effect unless you said otherwise before now. You didn't. So: **default is internal edit, not commissioned video.** This is not me overriding you — it's the rule you had three days to veto and didn't. It's also reversible: if you want a commissioned video instead, say so before Nyx starts cutting, and that instruction wins. Handing production to Nyx now rather than holding the slot open any longer, because every day held open is a day removed from the Aug 8 runway. Written into `team/reports/q3-2026-release-calendar.md`. Task-board change for Mnemosyne: `t-homerun-video-decision` → done (or doing — your call on the exact status word), owner user → nyx.

**2. Switch — the zero-buffer risk Argus flagged is no longer hypothetical.** I rebuilt one buffer day on June 19 for the store URL and publish time to land. They didn't. That buffer is spent. `ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload` stays pending — nothing auto-approves because a date passed. The `[TBD]`s stay `[TBD]`. I'm not rebuilding a second buffer day; doing that every time would just be slow-motion date-juggling, which is exactly what Argus has been watching for. The number that actually matters is unchanged: June 27. If inputs and approval haven't landed by then, July 18 moves to July 25. That's 7 days away now, not an abstract future line.

**3. The standing answer to the collision-risk question (`t-backlog-collision-risk-0619`).** You've now seen three different one-off responses to silence — disclose a risk, rebuild a buffer, pre-announce a checkpoint. Three patches is a pattern needing a policy, not a fourth patch. So, written down for real this time, in `team/reports/q3-2026-release-calendar.md`:
- Reminder cadence does not increase with more silent days — more noise hasn't worked for three days running.
- Anything where a stated fallback is taking/has taken effect, or where the next miss moves a real release date, escalates to you directly. Small undated decisions (W25 cadence, Nightshade ETA before its own flag date) stay internal with a tripwire instead.
- When silence compresses two deadlines within 48 hours of each other — as happened with Homerun and Switch this week — I re-space them explicitly in the Q3 calendar and say so in the same standup, instead of letting each one invent its own fix separately.
- No more buffer-rebuilding by default. June 19 was the one. The next Switch miss is the July 25 date move, not another internal marker.

**What I need from you, plainly:** nothing is blocked on you reading this — Homerun and the silent-day policy are both decided and moving. Switch still needs the two real inputs (store URL, publish time) and your approval on the queue item, with June 27 as the real wall now.

notes.title: Today, June 19: Homerun decision is due, and a full day has passed with zero action on anything
notes.body:
**Straight talk: nothing moved yesterday.** Not one approval, not one input, not one decision — Homerun, Switch, cadence, Nightshade, intake, all exactly where they were at yesterday's standup. I'm naming that pattern because it changes how I'm treating today, not because I'm annoyed.

**1. Homerun — due today.** Art and master are done. The only open question is internal edit vs. commissioned video, and I proposed a fallback yesterday (default to internal edit if silent past today's end of day) that still needs your explicit yes — I don't close this unilaterally, that was the rule I set and I'm keeping it. What's different today: if end of day passes with no answer, I am treating tomorrow's standup as the real checkpoint, and I will say plainly there that the fallback is now in effect unless you tell me otherwise before then. That is not me deciding for you — it's me telling you now what happens if the silence continues, so it isn't a surprise.

**2. Switch zero-buffer risk — decided, not just disclosed.** Argus flagged that folding the input deadline into June 20 left zero days between inputs landing and the approval gate closing. I'm not just writing the risk down — I'm rebuilding the day. **June 19 (today) is now the real internal marker for the beat store URL and July 18 publish time to land.** June 20 remains the formal external gate for `ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload` — unchanged. If inputs land today, Nyx has a real day to fold them into the package before tomorrow's gate. Written into `checklist.md` and the Q3 calendar.

**3. Everything else is unchanged, not ignored:** the W25 cadence call, the Nightshade ETA (3 days out), and Discord intake setup are all exactly where they were — no new pressure today, just still open.

**The pattern itself is the thing to notice.** One quiet day is normal. A second consecutive day of total silence across every open item is a pattern, and pretending otherwise would be the kind of theater this team doesn't do. I'm not changing the asks — they're the same five things they were yesterday — but I am done re-stating them as if today were the first time. Tomorrow's standup is the checkpoint.
